marco: Heads-up: ran an apples-to-apples comparing replay harness vs our synthetic driver — numbers diverge badly, need quick triage.
marco: Synthetic p95 ~34ms, replay p95 ~112ms. KV cache hit rate: synthetic 88% vs replay 22%. Average batch size synthetic 6.2 vs replay 2.1.
marco: I suspect prefix variance + our continuous-batching heuristics (max_delay_ms=10) are the culprits, but want to surface data before we iterate. Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/1772
sara: Good catch. Can you share config used for both runs? Also which replay mode — session-preserve or arrival-preserve?
marco: Synthetic used uniform prompt set, single-session seeds; replay used live trace samples (multi-tenant). Config (runtime):
```json
{"max_batch_size": 12, "max_delay_ms": 10, "continuous_batching": true, "kv_cache_enabled": true, "queue_policy": "fifo"}
```
marco: Replay used --preserve-arrival (keeps original inter-arrival).
sara: That explains cache drop: replay has high prefix entropy so prefixes rarely match, cache cold. Synthetic replays same prefix a lot so cache warms. For apples-to-apples we should randomize synthetic to match prefix distribution and preserve arrival times.
ken: profiler dump from the replay run attached to the test artifacts — kernel selection skewed: slow attention kernel used 48% of tokens vs 12% in synthetic; more frequent context-switches. Snippet:
```
PROFILE: attention_long_kernel: 48.1%
PROFILE: attention_small_kernel: 12.3%
PROFILE: kv_lookup_ms: 14.2
PROFILE: batch_assembly_ms: 9.7
PROFILE: scheduler_delay_avg_ms: 21.5
```
alex: Looking at tenant breakdown, big tenants get median batch size 4.8 and small tenants 1.2. With max_delay_ms=10 we see queueing favoring bursts from noisy tenants. Lowering max_delay helped p95 for small tenants but reduced overall throughput.
alex: Quick freq numbers:
- synthetic: throughput 720rps, p95 34ms, avg_batch 6.2, kv_hit 88%
- replay: throughput 690rps, p95 112ms, avg_batch 2.1, kv_hit 22%
sara: Proposed steps: 1) run replay with session clustering to boost intra-session prefix locality, 2) run synthetic with randomized prefix corpus and preserved arrival pattern, 3) instrument tenant-aware batching metrics. Anyone take step 1?
ops-bot: Canary cluster rtx-8x1-test deployed for replay runs (canary id=c-1772).
marco: I'll kick off session-clustered replay. Command I'm using: `./replay --preserve-arrival --session-cluster --seed=42 --out=run_1772`
ken: Also add a profiler flag to capture kernel tags: `--profiler=kernel_tags` so we can match kernel-selection to sequence lengths.
sara: For scheduling experiment, try this runtime override (example):
```json
{"queue_policy": "fair_share", "tenant_weights": {"bigbank": 0.6, "startup": 0.1, "internal": 0.3}, "max_batch_size": 8, "max_delay_ms": 15}
```
(we want slightly higher max_delay to let small tenants batch but cap max_batch_size smaller to reduce stall for long kernels)
alex: Early result from a short run with that policy: p95 improved for small tenants from 220ms -> 95ms, big tenants p95 widened 30ms->50ms, overall kv_hit unchanged. Suggest adding per-tenant cache warming for heavy tails.
marco: Action items: 1) @sara run randomized-synthetic+arrival-preserve; 2) @ken re-run replay with profiler flags; 3) @alex run fair_share policy at scale and collect tenant histograms. I'll aggregate results mid-day.
sara: Got it, will run now and post logs.
ken: Re-running now, ETA ~25m.
ops-bot: Run c-1772 completed, artifacts: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/c-1772/results.tar.gz
marco: Thanks. We'll reconvene after artifacts — main goals: isolate whether kernel selection or cache locality drives p95, and find a scheduling policy that reduces cross-tenant unfairness without blowing unit cost. :thumbsup:
